newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo drops after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo drops after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc eased on Thursday, after first-half profits proved no better than analysts expected, dealers said.
The stock was down 20p at 13.09-1/2 stg by 0937 GMT in volume of 3.5 million shares.
Dealers said the results were not enough of a positive surprise to enable the stock to build on its 40 percent rise since the end of 1996.

"Sterling is causing a problem and the stock is on a pretty 'ritzy' rating," said one dealer, "the company is managing the retreat from Zantac very well...but the stock has had a good run and there is just an element of caution there."

Pre-tax profit fell to 1.52 billion stg from 1.55 billion a year before, compared with forecasts mostly in a range between 1.48 billion stg and 1.55 billion. The company blamed sterling strength for much of the decline.
Yet some analysts remained positive on Glaxo's long-term outlook.
"Glaxo is set to become one of the strongest drug companies in the world by 1999," said BZW analyst Steve Plag. "The key message is that sales ex-Zantac were up a stunning 14 percent.
